subject: Post-call: PII governance, logging, and CMK options
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava.wilson@acme.com>; Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: PII governance, logging, and CMK options

Hi Ava / Samir — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before looping in your infra/security teams.

Call recap (30 min):
- Primary scope: serve inference for PHI/PII token classification + downstream analytics.
- Concerns raised: retention windows, redact-at-ingest, detailed access logging, and customer-managed key (CMK) requirement in EU.
- Redwood capabilities covered: in-transit TLS, at-rest encryption, BYOK support (KMS/HSM), fine-grained audit logs, configurable retention policies, and per-tenant isolation via Dedicated or Private deployment.

Open questions you asked us to confirm:
1) Can we limit raw-text retention to N days and only keep embeddings/metadata longer? (You called out 30d vs 365d scenarios.)
2) Can audit logs show token-level access for legal/audit review (time, user, API key, model, truncated request hash)?
3) For CMK: do we support both cloud KMS (customer key in your KMS) and HSM-backed key import for air-gapped deployments?

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a lightweight options doc that maps the three deployment patterns (hosted, dedicated, private) to retention, logging, and CMK choices. Please review the PDF (short) and flag which option set you want us to detail.
- Ava: please share your security contact and SOC/Security questionnaire if you want us to populate answers (we can do a first pass).
- Samir: would you prefer a follow-up technical call with our infra engineer to walk through HSM import vs. cloud KMS flows? We can do a 45-min deep dive next week.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-encryption-options-20261115.pdf (application/pdf, 412KB)]

Thanks — I’ll capture your selection and produce a mutual action plan.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0197

From: Ava Wilson <ava.wilson@acme.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII governance, logging, and CMK options

Thanks for the clear recap, Diego — that helps. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Retention: our baseline requirement is that raw text must be deletable within 30 days on request; derived artifacts (embeddings, anonymized metrics) can be retained up to 2 years. We need a documented retention policy and proof that deletions are irreversible for the raw blob.

2) Logging: we need immutable audit logs for read/write of raw inputs and any admin actions. Token-level logging is sensitive — we would accept request-level checksums plus metadata (timestamp, user, model id) instead of storing full tokens. The auditors want determinism so the logs need to be exportable in CSV/JSON.

3) CMK: preference is to manage keys in our existing EU cloud KMS (we run on a major cloud provider). HSM import is interesting but would add procurement time. Can you confirm if Redwood supports key rotation initiated from our KMS and how key revocation affects stored ciphertext?

Also attaching a snippet from our SOC pack showing log schema expectations — Samir can add anything I missed.

Ava
Head of Security, Acme HealthTech
[Attachment: acme-soc2-logging-extract.png (image/png, 75KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava.wilson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII governance, logging, and CMK options

Ava — great notes, thank you. Short answers below; Karthik and Marissa are looped to confirm policy/contract fit and technical details.

Retention/deletion:
- We support configurable retention per route. For Hosted customers we can set a 30-day raw-text retention policy and truncate/one-way-hash raw blobs on delete. For Dedicated and Private deployments you get full control (we’ll provide an API to trigger deletion and a compliance report). We will include a deletion proof (hash chain) in the compliance report for your auditors.

Logging:
- We can provide immutable append-only audit logs with export in JSON/CSV. We do not persist token streams in logs by default; instead we offer a deterministic request hash plus request metadata (timestamp, model_id, request_size, api_key_id, route). For customers needing token-level logs we provide an opt-in mechanism but it requires explicit config and additional retention controls.

CMK / KMS / HSM:
- For your cloud KMS: yes — Redwood supports BYOK where you store the master key in your KMS and Redwood keeps only AES-wrapped DEKs. Rotation initiated from your KMS is supported — on rotation we rewrap DEKs; ciphertext at rest remains decryptable provided the KMS key material is available.
- Key revocation: if the CMK is revoked/destroyed in your KMS, ciphertext becomes unrecoverable. We’ll document a recommended rotation and backup approach in the MOP.
- HSM import / air-gapped: supported for Private deployments; it requires exchange of a signing/attestation token and a short on-site ops window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik — can you prepare a short technical appendix (2–3 pages) showing the BYOK flow (cloud KMS rewrap timeline, key rotation steps, and sample audit log fields)?
2) Marissa — can you confirm if the contract needs an explicit clause for data destruction certification and whether we should include a 3rd-party attestation SLA for EU customers?
3) Ava/Samir — if agreeable, we’ll schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Karthik this week to walk through the BYOK flow and the audit log export.

I attached the options doc again for completeness.

Thanks,
Diego

[Attachment: redwood-encryption-options-20261115.pdf (application/pdf, 412KB)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava.wilson@acme.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII governance, logging, and CMK options

Ava — thanks for the specificity; that helps us scope the SOW. Quick notes from Legal/GT:

- Data destruction clause: we can include a contractual obligation to implement deletions within the window you request and provide a quarterly deletion attestation. For raw-text irreversibility, we’ll document the hash-chain proof and include it in the attestation language.
- Audit logs: we’ll commit to providing exports in CSV/JSON for the fields Diego outlined. If you opt into token-level logs we’ll add a separate appendix (higher retention costs and explicit approval needed).
- CMK: standard BYOK language will be included. Important: we must add a clause that clarifies customer responsibility for key backups and the irreversibility consequence of key destruction. We can also include a recommended playbook for rotation and key escrow options for enterprise customers if you want Redwood to hold an escrow copy under an indemnity arrangement.

Operationally: Diego — please coordinate the technical deep-dive with Karthik. Ava/Samir — once you confirm a time, we’ll send a calendar invite and an initial draft SOW and appendix within 3 business days after the call.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Marissa.Cole@redwood.ai
